questions.heading: The Budget Requirement Is Wrong Now, So the Change Modifies It
questions.stem: Finance changes the yearly budget rule. A teammate writes the new rule under ## ADDED Requirements, with a new name, and leaves the old requirement alone. What does the living spec hold after archive?

options.text: Both rules, as two requirements that contradict each other
options.says: Right: ADDED appends; the old requirement stays.

options.text: Only the new rule, since an ADDED rule replaces its match
options.says: The page: MODIFIED replaces; ADDED appends.

options.text: Only the old rule, since an ADDED rule is never merged
options.says: Archive appends every ADDED requirement to the living spec.

options.text: Neither rule, since archive refuses any ADDED budget rule
options.says: The page: adding it would leave two contradicting requirements, not none.

questions.heading: A MODIFIED Block Replaces the Whole Requirement, Scenarios Included
questions.stem: A MODIFIED block for Start window rewrites its text and lists one new scenario, leaving out the old 'A start outside the window is refused'. What happens?

options.text: The old scenario stays, since MODIFIED patches what it lists
options.says: The page: a MODIFIED block replaces the whole requirement.

options.text: It passes plain validation and fails strict, as a warning
options.says: The page: these are errors, not warnings; plain validation fails too.

options.text: Validation reports an error: the block drops a scenario
options.says: Right: OpenSpec refuses it in validate and in archive.

options.text: Archive keeps both versions of the requirement, side by side
options.says: The page: MODIFIED replaces the requirement on archive.

questions.heading: The Model
questions.stem: The carry-over is 30% and the yearly budget $2,000k. Which bounds does the page's model give each year's carry variable?

options.text: from -600 to 600, so a year may lend and may borrow
options.says: The page: the lower bound 0 forbids borrowing.

options.text: from 0 to 600: the cap above, and no borrowing
from 0 to 2,000, at most one whole year's budget
options.says: The cap is the carry-over percent of one yearly budget, here $600k.

options.text: fixed at 600 in every year, so all carry is used
options.says: The variable is bounded, not fixed; the row is an inequality.
